groups.name: Used non‑Google apps/services to find photos
groups.what: People reported using other apps/services (Apple Photos, Photobucket, Allo/Assistant, iNaturalist) instead of Google Photos to look for the picture.

groups.name: Only in another app/source, not in Google Photos
groups.what: Targets lived in third‑party sources (e.g., WhatsApp, Xender, InShot) so they weren’t findable in Google Photos.

groups.name: Sensitive/banned concept blocks search
groups.what: Queries were refused or heavily censored (e.g., grief, fat, race terms) making the photo unfindable.

groups.name: Wrong or upload-date metadata hides photos
groups.what: Photos were filed under transfer/upload or incorrect dates, so date-based finding failed.

groups.name: People/face search and grouping failures
groups.what: Face detection/grouping didn’t find key people or couldn’t be controlled, blocking people-based retrieval.

groups.name: Album‑scoped search missing
groups.what: Users wanted to limit search to a specific album or use album info (like addresses) but Photos only searched the whole library.

groups.name: Auto‑creations/Spotlights are ephemeral and hard to re‑find
groups.what: Surfaces like Spotlight videos/collages appear then disappear with no obvious place to retrieve them later.

groups.name: Hidden/Locked/Archived items hard to locate after moves/restores
groups.what: Items in special containers (Hidden, Locked/Safe Folder, Archive) or restored media were hard to find in the main library.

groups.name: Deep scrolling as fallback
groups.what: Users had to scroll far back through the timeline to locate items because targeted retrieval wasn’t working.

groups.name: Object/text queries return too few/zero matches
groups.what: Search recall was unexpectedly low for clear object/text queries (e.g., VIN, monkeys, cheese, serial numbers).

groups.name: Search returns irrelevant false positives
groups.what: Results surfaced clearly off‑target matches despite precise queries (e.g., brand/person misfires, wrong event, wrong food).

groups.name: Overwhelmingly similar photos/clutter impede finding
groups.what: Large volumes of near‑duplicate or similar photos made targeted retrieval impractical or demotivating.

finding: 12 candidate group(s) for the PM to approve or reject ([CTX] §8.3); none is applied until approved.
